chapter: Last years of the band and reflections
title: What the band earned and the steady grind
summary: The leaders made only slightly more than the sidemen, never got into big money, and compare their steady local work to bands living on buses.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: It really was. It was hard, but it was good. Now, the time we was at the Plantation, we didn't make no money to amount to anything. I mean, in this respect. Now, when the band was making $25 a week -- no, when the band was making $22 a week, we were making $30 a week. When the band went up to $25 a week, we were making $35 a week. That's what we were making, see. But we had to buy the music, you know what I mean. And we had to do a lot of other little things, too.
And even up to -- the ratio kept that way, see. The only time that we actually made a little extra money, and it

wasn't that much, because we didn't come out too much on those dates at the Polly Theater. When you figure the transportation, we had to pay for the transportation, and then, when you got back, we would clear after we'd pay your gasoline or your train fare, for somebody to come out here, because Agnes used to come — once we put her on the train, with the luggage and stuff, see. That was $45 round trip. Okay, we paid everybody off, and you're paying union dues out of that, you'd have about $200 left. And the other guys were making around about $100, $100 and some something like that.
Let's say it this way. We just never got into the big money.
We had quite a few guys with us that was fortunate to get out and make some of that money, but we never did.
We never did. We never did.
We didn't venture out from this town.

Well, I'll tell you, we did venture out from this town, but there were many bands that ventured out, and you look at them now, you see. We were consistent from year in and year out. We worked from one end of the year, man, to the other. From '40 on out, we worked right straight through, see.
And so, it was just a steady grind. It's like every- thing is turning slowly now, see. It was just a steady grind.

While the other guys on the road, like the Jimmy Lunsford band, those guys, they were sleeping in busses every night. And the kind of money they made, it wasn't all that big when they got through paying their room rents.
